meta.title: Data sources and methods
meta.description: Every data source Wayfare uses, when it was last updated, and how prices, rankings and weather rules are calculated.

title: Data sources and methods
intro: Wayfare only uses open data and APIs that allow it. We never scrape ticketing sites. Every result shows where it came from, and anything estimated or served from a fallback is clearly labelled.

gtfs.name: OTP Thailand GTFS (Mobility Database mdb-1831)
gtfs.use: Stations, routes, timetables and fares for skytrain, bus, boat and rail

fares.name: Published fare tables of each line
fares.use: Station-count fares when GTFS has no price

duffel.name: Duffel API (test mode)
duffel.use: Domestic flights when a token is configured

flights.name: Domestic flight schedule (fallback)
flights.use: Flight times and fare bands when Duffel is unavailable

rail.name: State Railway of Thailand timetable and fares

bus.name: Coach and van timetables posted at bus terminals

osrm.name: OSRM (OpenStreetMap road network)
osrm.use: Road distance and time for taxi, Grab, motorbike taxi, car and walking

roadFares.name: Taxi meter rates, motorbike taxi fare guide and Grab estimate

meteo.name: Open-Meteo Forecast API
meteo.use: Hourly rain chance, rainfall, temperature and wind, up to 16 days ahead

climate.name: Thai Meteorological Department climate normals 1991–2020
climate.use: Seasonal averages when no forecast exists yet

places.name: Curated places (coordinates from OpenStreetMap)
places.use: Key districts, airports and bus terminals

holidays.name: Thai public holidays 2026
holidays.use: Flight price adjustment over long weekends

gtfs.title: Skytrain, bus, boat and rail (GTFS)
gtfs.body: We import the national GTFS feed published by the Office of Transport and Traffic Policy and Planning (OTP) when the site is built and shrink it to what routing needs, so searches are fast and nothing is downloaded when you open the site. City routes are found with a RAPTOR-style, round-by-round transfer scan over this timetable.
gtfs.faresTitle: Fallback fares by number of stations
gtfs.faresBody: Used only when GTFS has no fare for a ride: base fare + fare per station, capped at the maximum (last checked {date}).

flights.title: Intercity: flights, trains, coaches and vans
flights.body: With a Duffel test-mode token we use flight offers from Duffel. Without one, or when it returns nothing, we use a fallback schedule labelled “estimated price”. Trains and coaches use publicly posted timetables; train departure times from Bangkok come from GTFS when available.
flights.formula: Flight price = base fare × day factor × advance-purchase factor × time-of-day factor
flights.band: Price range shown: {low}% to {high}% of the estimate

road.title: Roads and walking
road.body: Road distance and time come from OSRM on OpenStreetMap roads, cached per coordinate pair rounded to 3 decimals. If OSRM is unreachable we use straight-line distance × {detour} and label it as fallback data.

weather.title: Weather and warning rules
weather.body: We fetch the hourly Open-Meteo forecast at the place and time of each leg (up to 16 days ahead). For dates further out, or if the service is down, we use seasonal averages from the Thai Meteorological Department and say “no forecast yet”. Every warning comes with a reason and an alternative.

rain.then: Motorbike taxi “not recommended” and heavily penalised · outdoor walks over {walk} min: bring an umbrella · road time +{pct}%

heavy.when: Heavy rain ≥ {mm} mm/h or thunderstorm (weather codes {codes})
heavy.then: Motorbike taxi and walks over {walk} min removed from recommendations · boat warning · road time +{pct}% · {extra} min extra airport buffer

heat.then: Walks over {walk} min get a warning · “Most comfortable” favours air-conditioned rides

pm.then: Walks of {walk} min or more: wear a mask

pricing.title: How prices work
pricing.body: Every leg shows “about ฿X (range ฿A–฿B)” and adds up to a whole-trip total multiplied by the number of passengers. Skytrain, bus and boat use the published fare tables; road legs use the formulas below.
pricing.taxiFlag: Flag fall {fare} for the first {km} km
pricing.taxiExtra: Traffic waiting {wait} per minute · airport pickup +{airport} · trips over {km} km include expressway tolls {toll}
pricing.win: First {km} km {fare} · km {km}–5 add {to5} per km · over 5 km add {over5} per km · up to {max} km
pricing.grabTitle: Grab (estimated from distance and time, not an official price)

scoring.title: How we rank by what matters to you
scoring.body: We generate every feasible route, then keep only trips that no other trip beats on every count (Pareto) across price, total time, transfers and walking. They are then sorted by your choice. Trips marked “not recommended” because of the weather always come last. Changing your choice re-ranks instantly on your device.

fastest.title: Fastest
fastest.body: Shortest door-to-door time; ties go to the cheaper trip.

cheapest.title: Cheapest
cheapest.body: Lowest whole-trip cost × passengers; ties go to the faster trip.

value.title: Best value
value.body: Total price + time × value of time (default {rate}/h, adjustable in your profile) + weather risk × {risk} + transfers × {transfer} (per passenger).

comfort.title: Most comfortable
comfort.body: Comfort score 0–100: points off for transfers, walking, standing, no air-con, motorbike taxis and getting rained on; points added for sleeper trains.

scoring.filters: Extra filters: avoid motorbike taxi · walk at most X min · big luggage (no motorbike taxi or boat, walking time × 1.3) · budget up to ฿X · passengers

planner.title: Buffers, reliability and CO₂
planner.body: Every trip is split into walking · waiting · riding · transfers · buffers, and no trip connects faster than the minimum buffers below. In “arrive by” mode we work backwards to tell you when to leave home.
planner.reliability: Time reliability: skytrain “highly punctual” · road travel in rush hour “depends on traffic ± minutes” by distance

chain.title: Booking and refunds on Avalanche
chain.body: Bookable legs (flight, intercity train, coach, van, boat) are booked and paid in one transaction on Avalanche C-Chain. Money is held in escrow per leg and released to the operator when the ticket is scanned. If the operator cancels, the ticket holder is refunded in full immediately. Skytrain, taxi, motorbike taxi and walking legs are shown as “pay on the spot” and included in the total.
chain.demo: This demo runs on the Fuji test network with test money tUSDC (1 tUSDC = {rate}). Every bookable operator is a fictional name used for demonstration only.
chain.noShow: If the passenger does not board within 2 hours of departure, the operator receives that leg's fare.
chain.operatorCancel: Operator cancels the service: full refund, automatically.
